primitives.name: Throw Trajectory Alignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: He should keep the ball down, sending it in as nearly as possible on a line and just a little to the third-base side of home.
primitives.assumptions: Ball follows projectile motion with negligible air resistance; fielder throws on a straight line to target.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High-altitude throws or excessive lateral deviation cause misalignment with base path.

layer2.mapping: Optimal throw vector aligned with base path via lateral bias to third base, minimizing travel time to catcher.
layer2.telemetry: Distance error between projected throw and target base.

primitives.name: Ground Contact Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is remarkable how little the progress of a low-thrown ball is delayed by its once touching the ground; and it is also noticeable how convenient it is for a catcher to handle a ball taken on the bound in putting it on a runner.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t_bounce': 'time to first bounce (s)', 'v_ground': 'velocity after bounce (m/s)', 'd_total': 'total horizontal distance (m)'}
primitives.assumptions: Ball bounces elastically; ground contact does not significantly alter momentum direction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High bounce height or irregular surface causes unpredictable bounce behavior.

layer2.mapping: Minimizes delay in ball arrival by optimizing low-trajectory throws that strike ground near target.
layer2.telemetry: Time difference between direct and bounced throw arrival at target.

primitives.name: Lateral Bias Training
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the ball come at all on the other side of the plate, there is little chance of its catching the runner, and for this reason the fielder should be persistently trained to throw a trifle to the catcher's left.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'β': 'lateral offset (m)', 'θ_target': 'target angle relative to plate (rad)', 'θ_actual': 'actual throw angle (rad)'}
primitives.assumptions: Catcher is positioned to receive ball from left side of plate; lateral bias improves accuracy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Excessive lateral deviation beyond catcher's range results in missed throws.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to training protocol for consistent lateral targeting in baseball fielding.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of throws within ±10° of intended lateral offset.

These form a coherent mathematical framework where each primitive contributes to a unified model of throw effectiveness. The kinematic chain begins with initial velocity and launch angle, evolves through ground interaction dynamics, and concludes with spatial alignment to base targets. Dualities emerge in the trade-off between vertical arc and ground contact, and between precision and speed.
